ai.description: This 40–50 mm frog has a pointed snout and a dark, hourglass-shaped dorsal pattern. It features a distinct black stripe along each flank and a small, rounded body with short limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kalophrynus interlineatus* is best distinguished by the prominent, dark, hourglass-shaped marking on its back, which is absent in other similar Indian microhylids.
ai.habitat: *Kalophrynus interlineatus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found in leaf litter near seasonal pools at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Piebald Narrowmouthed Frog secretes a sticky, white mucus from its skin that can glue the jaws of potential predators shut.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kalophrynus interlineatus* breeds in water-filled tree holes during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs that develop into specialized larvae.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Kalophrynus interlineatus* occurs in Northeast India (Assam, Meghalaya, and Mizoram) at elevations ranging from near sea level to approximately 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Piebald Narrowmouthed Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched, insect-like chirps from shallow pools or flooded grasslands during the rainy season.
